title: Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng: Chiến thắng của đội tuyển Việt Nam là nguồn cảm hứng mạnh mẽ
content:
Ngay sau khi đội tuyển bóng đá Việt Nam giành ngôi vô địch Đông Nam Á, Thủ tướng Chính phủ Lê Minh Hưng đã gửi thư chúc mừng, biểu dương tới ban huấn luyện cùng đội tuyển bóng đá nam quốc gia Việt Nam.
Bày tỏ niềm vui mừng và xúc động khi chứng kiến đội tuyển thi đấu quả cảm, bản lĩnh trong trận chung kết trên sân vận động quốc gia Mỹ Đình, xuất sắc bảo vệ thành công ngôi vô địch Giải vô địch bóng đá Đông Nam Á (ASEAN Hyundai Cup 2026) Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng gửi tới ban huấn luyện cùng toàn thể đội tuyển lời chúc mừng nồng nhiệt và niềm tự hào sâu sắc nhất.
Theo Thủ tướng, hành trình thi đấu bảo vệ ngôi vô địch luôn là thử thách đầy cam go, nhưng ban huấn luyện và các cầu thủ đã thể hiện trọn vẹn bản lĩnh kiên cường, tính kỷ luật chiến thuật cùng tinh thần đoàn kết, khát vọng cống hiến mãnh liệt vì màu cờ sắc áo.
“Từng pha bóng lăn xả, từng khoảnh khắc thi đấu bền bỉ của các cầu thủ qua các trận đấu và nhất là trận chung kết lượt về trên sân Mỹ Đình đã đem về vinh quang cho thể thao, niềm tin, niềm hạnh phúc cho hàng triệu người hâm mộ trên khắp mọi miền Tổ quốc và kiều bào ta ở nước ngoài” - Thủ tướng bày tỏ.
Người đứng đầu Chính phủ nhấn mạnh, chiến thắng này tiếp tục khẳng định vững chắc vị thế hàng đầu của bóng đá Việt Nam trong khu vực.
Đây là kết quả của quá trình chuẩn bị công phu, sự chỉ đạo tài tình của ban huấn luyện, trực tiếp là huấn luyện viên trưởng Kim Sang Sik và ý chí không lùi bước của từng tuyển thủ.
Vì thế, Thủ tướng cho rằng chiến thắng hôm nay tiếp tục là nguồn cảm hứng mạnh mẽ, tiếp thêm động lực to lớn để thể thao nước nhà tự tin chinh phục những đỉnh cao mới ở tầm châu lục và thế giới trong tương lai.
Thủ tướng gửi lời chúc tới ban huấn luyện và toàn thể đội tuyển luôn dồi dào sức khỏe, giữ vững ngọn lửa nhiệt huyết, không ngừng nỗ lực rèn luyện để tiếp tục lập nên những kỳ tích mới, làm rạng danh Tổ quốc Việt Nam thân yêu.
Tối 26-8, đội tuyển Việt Nam đã hòa Thái Lan 2-2 ở trận chung kết lượt về ASEAN Cup 2026 trên sân Mỹ Đình (Hà Nội), qua đó bảo vệ thành công ngôi vô địch sau khi thắng chung cuộc 4-2 sau 2 lượt trận.
Đây là lần đầu tiên trong lịch sử, tuyển Việt Nam 2 lần liên tiếp vô địch giải đấu khu vực. Trước đó, "Những chiến binh sao vàng" đăng quang vào các năm 2008, 2018 và 2024. Với chức vô địch thứ 4, đội tuyển Việt Nam đã cân bằng số lần vô địch của Singapore và chỉ còn thua Thái Lan 3 lần.

title: DDL’s modern dairy farm boosting local milk production, reducing import reliance – Pres Ali
content:
As Guyana continues to push agricultural development to ensure the country’s food security, the Demerara Distillers Limited (DDL) state-of-the-art US$20 million dairy farm is being hailed for not only increasing local milk production but also its role in reducing national dependence on imported dairy. In a social media post on Sunday, President Dr Irfaan Ali lauded DDL for employing agricultural innovation at the facility, which he says is adding to the economic diversification of the country. “The Demerara Distillers Limited’s modern dairy farm at Moblissa is a strong example of the ongoing modernisation of agriculture and diversification of Guyana’s economy,” the Head of State said in a Facebook post. According to President Ali, “Through investments in technology and advanced farming methods, DDL is helping increase local milk production, reduce Guyana’s reliance on imports and enhance food security.” The Guyana Government has been encouraging the use of advanced farming techniques and modern technology to support agricultural development and national food security initiatives. DDL has said that its commercial dairy farm, located at Moblissa on the Soesdyke/Linden Highway, it is a strategic pillar in Guyana’s bid to lead the CARICOM 25 by 2025+5 food security initiative. By producing fresh, high-quality milk locally, the company aims to displace a significant portion of the tens of millions of US dollars currently spent annually on dairy imports. Only back in May, DDL announced the arrival of the first shipment of high-yield milking cows via a charter flight from the United States of America. Following strict biosecurity protocols, the 89 pregnant heifers were transferred from the aircraft to a fleet of flatbed trucks and transported to the Moblissa farm, where they acclimated in the state-of-the-art facility designed with modern climate-control amenities to ensure maximum comfort and productivity. Those pregnant heifers, which have since delivered, are now producing milk at commercial scale.
“Game-charger”
DDL’s Executive Chairman, Komal Samaroo, had stated back in May that this US$30 million investment is aimed as positioning the company as a “game-charger” in the local dairy industry. “We are not just building a farm; we are building a sustainable industry that will transform Guyana’s agribusiness sector and provide long-term food security for the region,” Samaroo had noted. The US multi-million-dollar dairy farm, the first of its kind in the Caribbean, will be supplying both the local and regional markets.
The facility stemmed from an agreement which was signed in February, 2023 by DDL subsidiary Tropical Orchard Product Company Limited (TOPCO) and the LR Group of Israel. Meanwhile, the Guyana Government has also rolled out a number of initiatives to support the advancement of the local dairy industry. Only back in December 2025, the Ministry of Agriculture handed over dairy stock to farmers as part of efforts to strengthen and expand Guyana’s dairy industry. Some 19 farmers had benefitted from that intervention – the first phase of the initiative. Agriculture Minister, Zulfikar Mustapha, at the time had called for livestock farmers to avoid a “tunnel vision” approach and embrace integrated systems across production. He had noted that more than $110 million has been expended to facilitate some 300 embryo transplants aimed at boosting dairy production and improving genetics nationwide. In addition to the dairy stock, farmers also received soilage to support improved feeding systems and sustainable production.

title: Ethiopia’s Peaceful Turn Carries a Continental Promise, Former African Leaders Say
content:
Ethiopia’s Peaceful Turn Carries a Continental Promise, Former African Leaders Say
Addis Ababa, August 24, 2026 (FMC) — For two former African presidents who have watched the continent’s struggles and aspirations from the frontlines of leadership, Ethiopia’s National Dialogue represents more than the conclusion of a national process. It is a moment of possibility—one that could strengthen Ethiopia’s own journey while sending a powerful message of peace, confidence and renewal across Africa.
At the closing of Ethiopia’s first National Dialogue Conference in Addis Ababa, former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta placed Ethiopia’s experience within a much larger African story. Their reflections carried a shared conviction: a peaceful, united and stable Ethiopia can become an important force for regional security, African prosperity and the continent’s continuing search for African solutions to African challenges.
For Obasanjo, the Dialogue has opened a path toward the kind of peace that can unlock Ethiopia’s immense potential. After four years of preparation, 46 days of deliberation and the participation of about 4,000 Ethiopians, he described the undertaking as historic and an example for Africa.
He stressed that peace cannot be partial or exclusive. It must be comprehensive, inclusive and sustainable, with space for those who were not part of the conference to contribute to the implementation of its recommendations.
For him, the value of the Dialogue will ultimately be measured by what follows it. Its recommendations, he argued, must move from paper into institutions, policies and practical action capable of strengthening national unity, security, development, dignity and prosperity.
But Obasanjo also looked beyond Ethiopia’s borders. He presented peace in Ethiopia as part of a wider architecture of common security and shared prosperity stretching from communities to the region, the continent and the wider world.
His message was especially striking when he linked Ethiopia’s stability to its economic possibilities. In his assessment, if Ethiopia secures peace, stability, unity and predictable conditions for development, it could double its GDP within seven years and become Africa’s largest economy, eventually joining the ranks of the developed nations within a generation.
That vision places Ethiopia’s peace not merely as an end in itself, but as a foundation for a larger national transformation with consequences far beyond its borders.
Kenyatta approached the same moment through the lens of Ethiopia’s extraordinary place in Africa’s history.
Standing in Addis Ababa, which he described as the living capital of the continent, he recalled how Ethiopia’s story has repeatedly intersected with Africa’s own search for dignity and self-determination.
He invoked the Battle of Adwa not simply as an Ethiopian military victory, but as an event whose message travelled across Africa and the African diaspora. He recalled Ethiopia’s stand against colonialism, its voice at the League of Nations and Addis Ababa’s role in the establishment of the Organization of African Unity.
For Kenyatta, that history gives Ethiopia a distinctive responsibility and opportunity in the continent’s present.
Yet his most compelling observation concerned Ethiopia’s people.
Moving in words from Tigray and the northern highlands through Afar, Somali areas, Harar, Oromia, central and southern Ethiopia, the southwest and Gambela, he painted a picture of a country whose richness lies in its extraordinary variety of peoples, cultures, faiths, traditions and systems of knowledge.
He pointed to Gadaa as an indigenous African tradition of governance and deliberation, arguing that Africa possesses political wisdom of its own. Ethiopia, in his view, carries an exceptional reservoir of that wisdom.
Rather than seeing diversity as a burden, Kenyatta urged Ethiopians to recognize it as a national resource—a tapestry whose strength comes from the many threads woven into it.
His message was equally clear on the country’s regional significance. Ethiopia’s peace, he said, is not a favor to its neighbors; it is a condition for their own stability. When Ethiopia chooses peace, he argued, trade routes can open, economies can become steadier, borders more secure and confidence across the continent can grow.
That is where the two former leaders’ messages converge.
Obasanjo looked toward the Ethiopia that could emerge from peace: more secure, prosperous, predictable and economically powerful. Kenyatta looked at the Ethiopia that Africa already knows: a historic center of African self-determination, a home of civilizations and an extraordinary meeting place of peoples and traditions.
Together, their reflections cast the National Dialogue as both a national achievement and a continental opportunity.
The message is ultimately one of confidence in Ethiopia’s capacity to turn dialogue into a lasting political and social foundation, and to transform its diversity, history and human potential into sources of strength.
For Africa, the stakes extend further. A peaceful Ethiopia can contribute more strongly to stability in the Horn of Africa, deeper regional cooperation and the continent’s pursuit of sustainable prosperity.
And for Ethiopia, the words of the two former presidents offer a warm reminder of the country’s place in the African imagination: not simply as a country navigating its own challenges, but as a nation whose peace, unity and progress can inspire confidence far beyond its borders.
As Kenyatta put it in his closing blessing, “May Ethiopia’s journey inspire Africa, may Africa’s unity inspire the world.”

title: Vilnius taps pasaulio diskgolfo sostine – į Lietuvą atvyks rekordinis skaičius rinktinių
content:
Rugsėjo 8–12 dienomis Vilnius taps pasaulio diskgolfo centru – sostinėje vyks 2026 metų WFDF pasaulio komandinis diskgolfo čempionatas (WFDF World Team Disc Golf Championships), rašoma pranešime žiniasklaidai.
Į Lietuvą atvyks 29 valstybių rinktinės, o šių metų čempionatas bus didžiausias ir tarptautiškiausias per visą varžybų istoriją.
Pasaulio čempionato kovos vyks Pūčkoriuose, Pavilnių regioninio parko teritorijoje įrengtose dviejose 18 diskgolfo krepšių trasose. Pagrindinė – „Piligrimo“ trasa – drieksis 2478 metrus ir ves sportininkus per atviras pievas, miškingus šlaitus bei Vilnios slėnio apylinkes.
Lietuvoje vyksiantis čempionatas taps išskirtiniu ir dėl kelių naujovių. Pirmą kartą turnyro istorijoje sportininkai varžysis dviejose – „Open“ ir „Masters“ – grupėse. Taip pat pirmą kartą WFDF organizuojamas pasaulio komandinis čempionatas vyks bendradarbiaujant su Profesionalų diskgolfo asociacija (PDGA).
„Tai aukščiausio lygio skraidančiojo disko sporto renginys Lietuvoje per visą istoriją. Ir tai didžiulis įvertinimas mūsų šaliai ir mūsų federacijai kaip organizatorei. Labai džiaugiamės šia gauta galimybe. Tikimės, jog tai ne tik prisidės prie diskgolfo kaip sporto plėtros, bet ir jo populiarumo augimo iš esmės. Žinoma, tokio masto renginys būtų sunkiai įmanomas be valstybės paramos“, – sakė organizacinio komiteto pirmininkas Ričardas Zareckis.
Komandiniame diskgolfe, skirtingai nei įprastuose individualiuose turnyruose, dėl pasaulio čempionų titulo varžosi valstybių rinktinės. Šalys tarpusavyje susitinka vienetų ir dvejetų mačuose, todėl svarbus ne tik individualus žaidėjų meistriškumas, bet ir komandos sudėtis, taktika bei gebėjimas rinkti pergales skirtinguose susitikimuose.
Tarp Lietuvoje kovosiančių šalių – JAV, Kanada, Australija, Japonija, Didžioji Britanija, Vokietija, Suomija, Prancūzija, Ispanija, Ukraina, kaimyninės Latvija, Estija ir Lenkija bei pati Lietuva. Į Vilnių atvyks ir tokių tolimesnių šalių kaip Kolumbija bei Pietų Afrikos Respublika atstovai.
Vilniaus čempionatas bus jau šeštasis pasaulio komandinis diskgolfo čempionatas. Pirmosios tokios pirmenybės 2016 metais surengtos Kanadoje, vėliau čempionatas vyko Didžiojoje Britanijoje, Estijoje, Kroatijoje ir Australijoje. 2026-aisiais renginys pirmą kartą persikels į Lietuvą.
Oficialios treniruotės Pūčkoriuose numatytos rugsėjo 6–7 dienomis, o pirmieji čempionato mačai prasidės rugsėjo 8-ąją. Tą pačią dieną Vilniuje vyks ir oficiali atidarymo ceremonija. Pasaulio čempionai paaiškės rugsėjo 12 dieną, po finalinių kovų bus surengta medalių įteikimo ir uždarymo ceremonija.
Dar prieš prasidedant čempionatui, rugsėjo 5 dieną, Vilnius suburs ir svarbiausius pasaulio diskgolfo organizacijų atstovus. Sostinėje vyks Pasaulinis diskgolfo forumas, kuriame WFDF,
PDGA, nacionalinių federacijų ir kitų organizacijų atstovai diskutuos apie sporto ateitį, tarptautinį bendradarbiavimą ir tolesnę diskgolfo plėtrą.
Čempionatą organizuoja Pasaulinė skraidančiojo disko federacija (WFDF), bendradarbiaudama su vietos organizaciniu komitetu, kurį sudaro „Team DiscCity“, Lietuvos skraidančiojo disko federacija ir Lietuvos diskgolfo federacija.
Lietuvos rinktinę sudaro:
Open: Andriejus Timofejevas, Arnas Lietuvninkas, Domas Šimkūnas, Gabrielius Gricius, Guoda Čaikinienė, Lina Umbrasaitė, Linas Strelkauskas, Matas Kievinas, Mireta Kievinė, Simona Laucevičienė, Tautvydas Gylys, Vytautas Lukas Paukštė.
Masters: Aurelijus Zinkevicius, Darius Žukauskas, Mindaugas Likas, Mindaugas Motiejaitis, Mindaugas Pošius, Miroslavas Jurgelevičius, Nadezhda Memelova, Oksana Žukauskienė, Raimondas Mikalkėnas, Sigita Puišienė, Svetlana Kobec, Vytenis Čukauskas.
Varžybos iš dalies finansuojamos valstybės biudžeto lėšomis, kurias administruoja Nacionalinė Sporto Agentūra.

title: I watched Vietnam Fall for the VinFast VF 3
content:
I watched Vietnam Fall for the VinFast VF 3

HANOI, Vietnam — I have driven through enough of Vietnam to get a good sense of what belongs on its roads. Over the past two years, my trips have taken me from Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City to Da Nang, Hai Phong and Can Tho, and through Dong Nai, Hung Yen, Khanh Hoa and Bac Ninh. Motorcycles are everywhere, of course, along with the familiar mix of taxis, buses, trucks and family cars.
But on my more recent trips, one car has become increasingly difficult to ignore: the VinFast VF 3.
It is not because the little electric car is particularly exotic. Quite the opposite. The VF 3 has become ordinary. I see them parked outside buildings, moving through traffic and waiting at charging stations. They appear in different colors, with different wheels and accessories, and with varying degrees of owner personalization.
That was not quite the case when I first encountered the car two years ago.
At the time, VinFast had just launched a campaign encouraging VF 3 owners to customize their cars. The company turned the idea into a competition, inviting owners to show what they could do with the small EV. The resulting cars were easy to notice because they looked different from one another. Some received new colors and graphics; others were fitted with accessories that gave them a more individual appearance.
What has changed since then is that personalization no longer looks like an event. It has become part of the way the VF 3 is seen on Vietnamese roads.
That tells us something about the car’s success that a sales chart cannot quite capture.
VinFast delivered 44,585 VF 3s in Vietnam in 2025, making it the company’s best-selling model for the year. The figure represented roughly a quarter of the 175,099 electric vehicles VinFast delivered in Vietnam during the year. The company continued to sell the model at a strong pace in 2026, delivering 5,564 units in July and bringing its year-to-date total to 29,345.
The numbers are impressive, but they do not fully explain why the VF 3 has become so recognizable. The car is small by any conventional measure, measuring about 3.2 meters long and 1.7 meters wide. It seats four and has a battery rated for up to 210 kilometers under the NEDC testing cycle. It was designed primarily as an affordable urban EV rather than as a substitute for a larger family car.
That positioning makes considerable sense in Vietnam. Motorcycles and scooters remain the country’s dominant form of everyday personal transportation because they are inexpensive, maneuverable and easy to park. Moving from two wheels to four usually means accepting a substantially larger and more expensive vehicle. The VF 3 offers a different proposition: a small enclosed car that occupies relatively little space and can handle the short urban journeys that make up much of daily travel.
The design helps, too. The VF 3 is upright and deliberately simple, with enough visual character to stand out without looking expensive or overly sophisticated. It has the proportions of a small city car but enough room for a family to use it for ordinary trips. That simplicity also leaves plenty of scope for owners to change its appearance.
VinFast appears to have recognized that potential early. Its 2025 customization competition offered a 650 million Vietnamese dong prize pool and attracted owners who treated the VF 3 as something more than transportation. The modified cars ranged from colorful urban versions to builds with roof racks, additional storage and more adventurous styling.
What I find more interesting now is what happened after the campaign ended. The cars I see today are not simply factory-standard vehicles with a different badge. Owners have continued adding their own touches, and because there are so many VF 3s on the road, those individual choices have become part of the visual character of the model.
That is a useful distinction. A vehicle can sell in large numbers because it is inexpensive and practical, but that does not necessarily mean owners become attached to it. The VF 3 seems to have crossed that line in Vietnam. People are not merely buying a small EV; many are treating it as something they can personalize.
The effect becomes more apparent when you see the car in different parts of the country. In Hanoi, it fits into dense traffic dominated by two-wheelers. In Ho Chi Minh City, it disappears and reappears among a much larger mixture of vehicles. In Da Nang and Nha Trang, it looks equally at home in the urban and tourism economy. Further north, in places such as Hai Phong, Hung Yen and Bac Ninh, I have seen the same basic pattern: the VF 3 is simply part of the traffic.
That geographical spread matters. This is not a phenomenon restricted to a single city or an enthusiast gathering. The car has become common enough that its presence is no longer remarkable.
There is an important business lesson in that for VinFast and for other EV manufacturers. Electric cars are often sold through technology: battery capacity, charging speed, range, software and performance. Those specifications matter, but they do not necessarily create affection for a vehicle. The VF 3 has a simpler proposition. It is affordable, easy to recognize, practical in crowded cities and sufficiently distinctive to give owners something to work with.
VinFast has also created a domestic ecosystem around its EVs, including charging infrastructure and electric taxi and ride-hailing operations. Its larger Green models serve commercial fleets, while the VF 3 is primarily associated with individual ownership. That distinction is becoming visible on the road. The Green vehicles look like working transportation; the VF 3s increasingly look like people’s cars.
That may be the more important story behind the model’s sales.
Vietnam is moving from a transportation culture dominated by motorcycles toward a more diverse mix of electric cars, taxis and commercial vehicles. The transition does not require every motorcyclist to suddenly buy an electric SUV. A small, relatively inexpensive car such as the VF 3 can provide an intermediate step for people who want four wheels without giving up the practicality that made motorcycles so dominant in the first place.
I have watched that change over several trips to Vietnam. Two years ago, the customized VF 3s caught my attention because VinFast had turned personalization into an event. Today, when I see a brightly colored or accessorized VF 3 moving through traffic, I don’t assume it is part of a promotion. It is more likely simply somebody’s car.
That is probably the clearest measure of how far the VF 3 has come.
It started as a new model that attracted attention because it was small and different. In Vietnam today, it has become familiar enough to be part of the landscape, while the individual touches added by owners have given an otherwise simple electric car a character of its own.
